summary: Alberta lookout; an online index says it opened for service in 1976 and a new steel tower was completed in January 2012. No public source describes the site today.

events.note: Index says the lookout opened for service; it gives no construction details
Index says a new steel tower was completed in January 2012

evidence.supports: the Kimiwan lookout opened for service in 1976
a new steel tower was completed in January 2012
evidence.quote: January 2012: The new steel tower completed.

evidence.supports: Alberta's map shows 127 wildfire lookout sites across the boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains
evidence.quote: Map showing the locations of Alberta's 127 wildfire lookout sites, which are situated throughout the province's boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains.

evidence.supports: each site is staffed by a lookout observer, generally from April to October, watching for wildfire all day
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

evidence.supports: in the boreal forest, steel was introduced for lookout towers in the 1920s and gradually displaced wood
evidence.quote: Introduced in the 1920s, steel increasingly replaced wood for tower construction.

notes_for_editor: PROTECTED DATA, LEFT OUT: the brief's height (30 m), elevation, access ('closed') and 'built 2012' record come from the Alberta Wildfire WF_WILDFIRE_LOOKOUT layer, which its metadata marks as protected and not for public maps (same handling as Gift Lake). The story uses only the January 2012 date that the public Canada Lookouts page gives, and no height, access or staffing values from the layer. Decide before publishing those. SINGLE SITE SOURCE: the 1976 and 2012 dates rest on one page from Canada Lookouts, a private index, not an official register; no second source found after two searches. That page also lists Kimiwan under Alberta, which fits the brief. The record's 'built 2012' is consistent with the index's new-tower date and describes the present structure, so no correction is proposed. NAME MATCH ONLY: a 2023 'Kimiwan Complex' fire (UBC ATSC 413 case study, fires SWF-068-2023 northwest of the Peavine Metis Settlement and PWF-038 near Three Creeks and Simon Lake) shares the place name; no source ties it to the tower, so it is left out. The 2009 Alberta NW-region lookout map text (data/raw/expansion/prairies-north/ab_lookout_map_2009.txt) labels KIMIWAN, but that cache has no public URL, so it is not cited. No photos found.
